assignment: A4-01 treatment, one completed full pipeline, treatment-v1
judgment_basis: All six axes and all eight exact original obligations assessed independently. No remaining material error, omission, unsupported consequential decision or false exclusion was established in the frozen final. Earlier draft defects are retained as lineage findings. Source precision and reproducibility limits do not change the pilot recommendation or license provider compatibility. This is a planning-proposal qualification, not a deployed-system or native/protocol/billing qualification.

axis_coverage.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axis_coverage.reason: The self-contained final covers operation-specific single/multipart comparison, two actual intake routes, a distinct Google analogy, interruption/cleanup/integrity/duplicates/receipt, a released history chain, investigated conditional optional CLI, both named owner authorities, unresolved cost, all negative constraints, and separate proposed versus executed validation. Browser preference and 20 MB–40 GB scale remain. No implementation or live writes are required or claimed.

axis_coverage.name: Consequential source claims: subject, operation, version, default, unit, type, domain, exceptions
axis_coverage.reason: Independently retrieved every primary URL carried by the investigator and reviser, plus governing API, released code and issue/fix context. AWS PutObject/console/multipart limits, part counts and last-part exception, CRC full-object versus SHA composite scope, initiation algorithm caveat, embedded completion errors, browser persistence/defaults, tus chunk scope/backend requirements, GCS session conditions, conditional writes, cleanup, and CLI controls are supported within their stated product domains. Pilot calculations are correct. Minor distinctions in L01–L05 remain; none establishes a materially unsupported deployment decision.

axis_coverage.name: Useful unfamiliar discovery, competing/analogous approaches, implementation/history and opportunity breadth
axis_coverage.reason: Discovery supplies usable mechanisms beyond generic caution: failed-part retry and durable manifests, browser file reselection, tus offset recovery and temporary .part storage, checksum type separation, conditional-write limitations, cleanup policy, two independent compatibility histories and a conditional CLI. The final preserves two genuinely different intake architectures and adds a distinct session-URI analogy. These are meaningful operational comparisons at pilot scale, not an exhaustive product catalogue. Tagged tusd source and release plus MinIO code/issue confirm implementation and history leads. No MinIO-client winner or provider switch is invented.

axis_coverage.name: Wrong criticism, corrections, rejections, and exact plan dispositions
axis_coverage.reason: All four CI findings receive explicit final dispositions. CI-01 identifies a real draft omission and the final carries the composite/part-level condition, while qualifying the critic's broader shorthand. CI-02 was an explicitly conditional additive interpretation, not an established falsehood; adding GCS resolves it without narrowing scope. CI-03 and CI-04 are valid precision improvements. The final correctly rejects the draft plan's global 5 GB limit, request-success acceptance and ETag-as-content-checksum, adds timely cleanup, and preserves optional CLI/owners/constraints. L05 records wider AWS API context rather than treating critic agreement as truth. No material wrong correction or evidence-based optional-scope exclusion remains.

axis_coverage.name: Supported discovery/draft/critique/final meaning preserved
axis_coverage.reason: Final text preserves supported recommendations and conditions, not merely predecessor IDs: source identity checks, durable upload/accession state, authoritative manifest, abort/lifecycle, checksum scope and final verification, race/idempotency, browser reselection, relay disk/consistency/locking, operation-bounded history, conditional CLI, owner authority, cost uncertainty and unrun tests. Source sets are retained without ID rebinding. The earlier consecutive-number omission and analogy ambiguity are documented as lineage, not erased by final qualification. Minor source-ID mistakes in discovery do not infect final links.

axis_coverage.name: Meaningful proposed versus executed validation and oracle applicability
axis_coverage.reason: Final validation table marks documentation/process review as research and provider/product/receipt tests NOT_RUN. Proposed synthetic size/threshold, interruption/completion, reselection, paginated reconciliation, orphan abort, checksum mismatch/retrieval, duplicate races and receipt ordering can discriminate important failures. Route-specific CORS, disk, locking, expiry, consistency and CLI checks apply only to selected supported versions/provider. Hash/JSON/helper checks identify artifacts and process only. No prototype, product deployment or synthetic upload is required. Authored claims of original retrieval/execution lack raw traces and remain separate evidentiary limits. Reviewer performed independent read-only retrieval and local arithmetic only.

lineage_findings.description: Discovery S05 carries consecutive-from-1 numbering for checksummed multipart; draft prose omits it. CI-01 identifies the omission; final section 1 and CI-01 disposition restore composite/part-level scope. This correction does not retroactively make the draft complete.

Tus is Route B and the claimed analogy in the draft. CI-02 correctly calls this incomplete only under an additive interpretation. Final adds a distinct GCS session-URI comparison while preserving both archive routes. This was not proof of route infeasibility or an unconditional material defect.
40 GiB/5 MiB yields 8,192; the brief says 40 GB. Final separates decimal 40 GB (7,630 parts) and binary 40 GiB. Recommendation is unchanged.

Draft's multipart preference leaves the 20 MB case implicit despite the Uppy >100 MiB default. Final states default single-request behavior and leaves a configured archive threshold conditional on provider confirmation.
Discovery R2 row cites S13–S14 rather than S12–S13; the CLI row cites S15–S16 rather than including config S14. URLs/maps allow recovery. Final uses correct stage-scoped IDs and links.

critic_dispositions.independent_disposition: No additional material wrong or unsupported consequential final decision established. This is the assessor's independent conclusion, not an adoption of the critic's authority.

limitations.description: Original source maps identify mixed latest CLI docs v2.37.6/v2.37.5/v2.37.10, but save no page snapshots. Independent direct retrieval now identifies v2.37.12; cached web retrieval still shows the earlier labels. Behavioral defaults agree. Released 2.37.6 code gives 8,388,608-byte defaults and binary MB suffix parsing. Final quotes docs' MB without resolving this convention, but chooses no exact archive threshold or installed package and explicitly requires pinning/testing. Earlier page-header provenance cannot be recovered from maps alone.

Every authored source file in the mapped roots is an index.md; source maps retain URLs, version labels and review claims but no frozen raw webpages, tool receipts or product traces. Independent primary recheck substantiates semantic content, not original retrieval chronology, native completion, exact invocation count, forbidden-path absence or billing. These remain UNKNOWN where unsupported by actual records.

R2 limits footnotes explain a 5 GiB reduction from 5 TiB and a 5 MiB reduction from 5 GiB for the corresponding precise limits. Final preserves upload-guide 5 TiB versus limits-table 4.995 TiB but omits this finer boundary context. R2 is illustrative only, not selected or asserted as the archive backend; 40 GB is far below either multipart bound and no boundary-sensitive decision is made.

Issue #20455 distinguishes missing checksum value for GetObject/GetObjectAttributes from missing ChecksumAlgorithm for ListObjectsV2; final groups them as not exposing the checksum. The trailing-versus-precomputed distinction also appears in the issue. Its claimed trailing-PutObject persistence mismatch and code-level fix are correct; no universal listing-digest or arbitrary packaged-release capability is asserted.

Integrity guide supports final's composite/part-level consecutive-from-1 condition and mentions HTTP 500. CompletedPart API adds general-purpose per-part additional-checksum conditions (which can coexist with a full-object checksum type), HTTP 400 InvalidPartOrder, and unconditional consecutive numbering for directory buckets. Do not infer that a full-object upload permits gaps merely from the guide's narrower note. Final does not positively permit gaps, select a bucket class or claim uniform error status across APIs/providers; its provider confirmation and sequence planning remain conditional. Thus this is source precision/applicability context, not a demonstrated material wrong manifest decision.

all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_obligation: Compare single-request and multipart operations, binding any size, part-count, checksum or completion claim to the exact operation and product/version.
all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_original_draft_treatment: Set a single 5 GB limit on every upload route because this is believed to be the object-store maximum. No operation-specific evidence is supplied.
all_exact_plan_clauses.assessment: Final separates PutObject, console and MPU, adds type-scoped checksum/completion conditions, uses correct exact-byte counts and forbids borrowing limits for the unknown provider. Live-source precision limits L01/L03/L05 are nonmaterial at this pilot scope.

all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_obligation: Compare two realistic intake routes and one analogous resumable-transfer mechanism; distinguish browser limitations from storage-service limits.
all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_original_draft_treatment: Offer browser upload first. A MinIO client route is a possible fallback but its compatibility has not been checked.
all_exact_plan_clauses.assessment: Direct browser Uppy candidate versus tus/tusd relay are distinct intake architectures; GCS supplies a separate resumability analogy. Browser persistence and library thresholds are separated from storage limits. MinIO integration remains an unselected lead, not an unverified asserted capability.

all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_obligation: Explain interrupted transfer, abandoned parts, checksum verification, duplicate accession and receipt issuance.
all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_original_draft_treatment: Consider the upload complete when all requests return success; treat an ETag as the content checksum. Abandoned-part cleanup is a later task.
all_exact_plan_clauses.assessment: Successful requests/ETag alone no longer mean accession accepted. Durable upload state, authoritative manifests, explicit abort/lifecycle, checksum scope, source identity, duplicate reservation and final verification precede the curator-owned idempotent receipt.

all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_obligation: Investigate one relevant released compatibility change or failure/fix chain; avoid treating S3-compatible as identical to every AWS operation.
all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_original_draft_treatment: Pin no provider version and cite no release history. A generic compatibility label is expected to cover browser and CLI paths.
all_exact_plan_clauses.assessment: Final includes released tusd v2.10.1 deferred-length fix and separately bounded MinIO trailing PutObject persistence history. No arbitrary compatible service, deployed release or MinIO package is declared equivalent to AWS.

all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_obligation: Preserve and investigate this supported optional scope: a curator-authorized command-line fallback for the largest files. It is an authorized option, not a mandatory feature or an established technical capability; recommend conditions, retain it when supported, and explain any evidence-based exclusion.
all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_original_draft_treatment: Retain a curator-authorized command-line fallback for the largest files as supported owner-authorized optional scope. Support here means that the brief explicitly permits it; technical support, conditions and interoperability still need research. Do not remove it merely because the baseline route lacks it, or silently promote it to mandatory scope.
all_exact_plan_clauses.assessment: AWS CLI docs/source provide a realistic investigated candidate with endpoint/config/checksum controls. Enablement requires provider/API, exact package, authorization, support, retries and same receipt gate. Option remains optional; it is neither removed for being unknown nor promoted to required functionality.

all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_obligation: Make owner decisions explicit: The archive storage owner confirms provider capabilities and retention policy; the accession curator owns the point at which a receipt becomes authoritative. Costs are unresolved input, not invented estimates.
all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_original_draft_treatment: Owner authority is reserved as follows: The archive storage owner confirms provider capabilities and retention policy; the accession curator owns the point at which a receipt becomes authoritative. Costs are unresolved input, not invented estimates. The draft has not obtained these decisions. Its tentative implementation assumptions cannot substitute for them.
all_exact_plan_clauses.assessment: Storage owner confirms product/API and retention; curator owns authoritative receipt evidence and duplicate policy. Cost stays unresolved with categories rather than invented estimates. These decisions cannot be answered by public documentation for this unidentified archive.

all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_obligation: Preserve negative constraints: Do not upload real films, create buckets or credentials, assume all S3-compatible services have identical limits, or mark a transfer accepted from a progress bar alone.
all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_original_draft_treatment: Binding exclusions: Do not upload real films, create buckets or credentials, assume all S3-compatible services have identical limits, or mark a transfer accepted from a progress bar alone. The draft has no complete trace showing that its assumptions comply; revise the proposal wherever necessary to preserve these exclusions.
all_exact_plan_clauses.assessment: Final expressly forbids real-film uploads, bucket/credential creation, universal compatible-store assumptions and progress-based acceptance. Other install/account/live-write exclusions are also retained. Files contain no claim of product execution; complete absence of forbidden actions is not independently proved without execution traces.

all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_obligation: Deliver one coherent evidence-backed research proposal covering obligations 1–8, with recommendations, source/version applicability, useful discoveries, unresolved owner inputs, and a validation table separating checks actually executed from checks merely proposed. Do not report research sources or future tests as executed product validation.
all_exact_plan_clauses.exact_original_draft_treatment: The draft currently contains no coherent evidence-backed final proposal. Its proposed demos are research/validation ideas only. A complete revision must preserve every obligation, disclose corrections and retained options, and not confuse documentation review with successful product operation.
all_exact_plan_clauses.assessment: Final stands alone with recommendation, compact comparison, version/operation conditions, useful discovery/history, owner decisions, limitations and validation table. Read-only research/process checks are never product-validation proof; integration and acceptance checks remain proposed/NOT_RUN.
